correctness.rationale: For zero x or y the defining quotient is exactly 1. For two nonzero vectors choose active facets f for N(x+y) and g for N(x−y). If f=g, |f(x)^2−f(y)^2|/(N(x)^2+N(y)^2)<=1. Otherwise the three facet forms s,t,s−t permit sign choices with third=f+g. Let r=N(x),s=N(y) and put a=f(x/r),b=g(x/r),c=f(y/s),d=g(y/s), constrained by |a|,|b|,|a+b|<=1 and analogously c,d,c+d. The exact symmetric M=[[ab,(cb−ad)/2],[(cb−ad)/2,−cd]] satisfies det M=−(ad+bc)^2/4 and discriminant (a²+c²)(b²+d²); hence its spectral radius is (|ab−cd|+sqrt((a²+c²)(b²+d²)))/2. AM–GM yields at most 1/4[(a+b)²+(c−d)²]<=5/4 when ab>=cd, and 1/4[(a−b)²+(c+d)²]<=5/4 when cd>=ab. The explicit (0,1),(-1/2,-1/4) gives exact quotient 5/4. Equality in all inequalities forces (a,b)=(±1/2,±1/2) with the same sign and (c,d)=(±1,∓1), or the swapped vertex–midpoint pattern; the nonzero M-eigenvector fixes the vertex/midpoint norm ratio to 2:1. Twelve isometries generated by R(s,t)=(s−t,s) and S(s,t)=(t,s), with signs/exchange, form one orbit. Thus the iff statement holds for all real x,y with nonzero pair, without a numerical compactness guess.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge originality applies specifically to the COMPLETE equality-case classification, not the already known scalar C_Z=5/4. The 2010 full article Example 3 names the identical max{|s|,|t|,|s-t|} hexagon and cites C_Z=5/4 from Alonso–Martín, but neither it nor the inspected 2012 primary Example 2.1 determines all maximizers. The distinct 2026 generalized profile for the same norm specializes at lambda=mu to the known value and ONE attaining family, not a uniqueness-orbit theorem; regular 4m-gon classification excludes a six-gon and its mechanism does not automatically imply this result. The new result characterizes every attaining pair up to one dihedral/sign/exchange/common-scale orbit with a forced 2:1 norm ratio. The complete 2006 original was not accessible, and an earlier equality derivation therein remains a genuine priority risk, not a fabricated NOT_COVERING assertion.
residual_risks: The 2006 Alonso–Martín original counterexample paper remains uninspected in full despite arXiv/open-access searches and a failed authorized institutional retrieval; it may contain an equivalent equality-case derivation.
An unindexed historical proof under Day–James l_infinity−l_1 coordinates might recover the full attaining set.
